review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. North Pacific survey models and NOAA migration-corridor analysis support marine SST relevance; configured SST band is warmer than the modeled preference, and bathymetry is a weak pelagic proxy.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 2-4 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for chum salmon.
factors.value_notes: Langan et al. (2024) modeled chum marine preferred SST at 1.3-12.6 °C (80% HDI), core 2.8-9.3 °C, median 7.1 °C and modal 5.8 °C. A 2025 NOAA-authored migration-corridor study also uses SST-based thermal suitability for western Alaska chum and identifies low suitability at warm/cold migration margins. The configured 6-14 °C range and 8-12 °C ideal are shifted warm and omit much of the colder modeled preference. These are North Pacific stock/migration results, not a universal local catch curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for chum salmon.
factors.value_notes: Chum migrate through estuarine, coastal and open-ocean habitats during their marine phase; NOAA describes offshore migration across the North Pacific. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth. No reviewed source validates the configured 0-60 m seabed band as a universal preference; retain only as a weak shelf/coastal context proxy.
